title: Research: no two-target UT4 word has n_b=7 with middle ranks (2,2) (n_b=7 open; no new kappa)
body:
## Change and mathematical scope

Narrows the remaining gate left by [#3887](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/3887). In the explicit `F_2[UT_4(F_2)]` central-target alphabet of [#1662](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/1662), no legal word realizing two central targets — of any finite length, on any finite restored dirty workspace — has exactly seven paid `b` calls with middle ranks `(rank X, rank Y) = (2, 2)`, under the same unrestricted side-zero profile reduction used there.

At `n_b = 7` the #1662 rank bound permits patterns `(2,2)`, `(2,3)`, and `(3,2)`. The `(2,2)` slice still places every middle coupling in a fixed 2-plane, so interior dirty contractions cannot touch the side or `abc`/`cba` coefficients. Those equations reduce to a two-role unrestricted-profile census.

The census enumerates all 49,686 GL2-minimal zero-sum length-7 middle sequences, keeps the 49,140 with ranks exactly `(2,2)`, builds every side-zero transport key via a 3+4 meet-in-the-middle, and pairs keys for `abc = cba = I_2`. **Zero pairs survive.** A low-rank control with ranks `(1,2)` still produces pairs, so the screen is not empty by accident.

**Scope.** Middle ranks `(2,2)` only. Patterns `(2,3)` and `(3,2)`, and unrestricted `n_b = 7`, are left open. This does not claim that every `n_b = 7` word is impossible, does not restate the unit-tariff minimum 16 from [#1816](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/1816), and does not reprint the `n_b = 6` census. No supplier or κ change.

**No new kappa.** Selected κ stays `0.001672660197076918`.

## Task and overlap

- Package: `research/ut4-two-target-nb7-ranks-22/`
- Tip: `4995b0ce91c163de821a5d117c6e5a5289c12172`
- Base: `20ecf2891d80b5acf18d980b2164fb44ea7faa90`
- Scope: **refined** — decide the `(2,2)` slice of `n_b = 7` only

Closest prior: [#3887](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/3887) (`n_b = 6` impossible). The length-7 `(2,2)` census is the slice that PR left open; it is not forced by the length-6 result, because at `n_b = 7` the rank bound newly admits `(2,3)` and `(3,2)`.

## Validation

```sh
python3.12 -I -B research/ut4-two-target-nb7-ranks-22/verify.py
python3.12 -I -O -Werror -B research/ut4-two-target-nb7-ranks-22/verify.py
python3.12 -I -B research/ut4-two-target-nb7-ranks-22/independent.py
python3.12 -I -B research/ut4-two-target-nb7-ranks-22/test_package.py
python3.12 -B scripts/research_package.py --package research/ut4-two-target-nb7-ranks-22
```

Expected:

```text
PASS_UT4_TWO_TARGET_NO_NB7_RANKS_22 key_pairs=0 middles=49140
PASS_UT4_TWO_TARGET_NO_NB7_RANKS_22_INDEPENDENT key_pairs=0 keys_sum=46169088
PASS_UT4_TWO_TARGET_NO_NB7_RANKS_22_PACKAGE_CONTROLS checks=7
PASS_REGISTERED_RESEARCH_PACKAGE research/ut4-two-target-nb7-ranks-22 outcome=negative-result
```

Default verify is read-only. Admission uses `need()` and still fires under `-O`. A temporary copy of `CERTIFICATE.json` with corrupted pairs is rejected, and duplicate JSON keys are rejected. `independent.py` does not import `verify.py`.

## Open next questions

1. Does any two-target word have `n_b = 7` with middle ranks `(2,3)` or `(3,2)`? A middle rank of 3 escapes the fixed 2-plane argument used here.
2. Does any two-target word have unrestricted `n_b = 7`? That needs a dirty-role argument beyond the side-zero reduction.
